content:
This week, Apple continues to expand its Apple Sports app, adding more football league coverage and giving tennis fans new ways to follow major tournaments. Here are the details of the latest update.

Apple Sports adds football leagues and tennis schedules

When the Apple Sports app first launched, the experience was quite limited in terms of both available regions and supported sports.

Since then, the app has continued to grow on both fronts, now reaching more than 170 countries and regions, with more sports, leagues and events being added over time.

For example, earlier this year, Apple Sports expanded coverage to 90 countries and rolled out several new features built around the FIFA World Cup.

This week, Apple Sports is updated again, adding Australia's A-League Men, the Egyptian Premier League, the Israeli Premier League and the South African Premier League to its football coverage.

In addition, Apple says the app now lets tennis fans "follow live draws... including brackets for Grand Slams and 1000-level events," allowing users to "see matchups and results for each round at a glance."

Here are the full release notes for Apple Sports 4.4:

Football coverage continues to expand with the addition of Australia's A-League Men, the Egyptian Premier League, the Israeli Premier League and the South African Premier League. Tennis fans can now follow live draws on Apple Sports, including brackets for Grand Slams and 1000-level events, making it easy to view matchups and results for every round.

Do you use Apple Sports? Let us know in the comments.
